A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MRAG-BENCH. Their main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 LVLMs and human participants, along with retriever comparisons and analyses in Sections 3–4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, human results, retriever comparisons, and example-count experiments.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and retrieval-augmented answering procedure remain unchanged. No model architecture, algorithm component, or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,353 questions and 16,130 images across nine scenarios, with unchanged data sources and evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same 14 LVLMs and human/random references; Table 4 retains the same two-model comparison. Appendix C retains CLIP, MagicLens, E5-V, and VISTA.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, retrieval counts, generation settings, human evaluation protocol, and the 892-question example-count study are unchanged. The new CLIP statement clarifies the existing setup without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The visual-versus-textual knowledge comparison, retriever analysis, ground-truth example-count study, and qualitative error analysis retain the same experiments and supporting displays.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 5 retain averaging across three random seeds for sampling ground-truth examples. Statistical and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 4.1 corrects LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave’s ground-truth image-over-text advantage from 11.09% to 11.90%. This matches the unchanged Table 4 accuracies of 52.99 and 41.09, a difference of 11.90 percentage points. Other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The query, retriever, and model formulation in Section 2.1 and the scenario definitions are unchanged. Neither version contains a theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about the benefits of visual knowledge and LVLMs’ limited ability to exploit retrieved information.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning noisy retrieval, proprietary versus open-source models, possible position bias, and difficulties using many images remain unchanged. The corrected percentage does not alter these interpretations.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly states that CLIP is consistently used across all models. v1 identified CLIP for the Section 4.1 comparison but lacked this explicit all-model clarification. Appendix instructions, prompts, and access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography content, and research positioning in Section 5 are unchanged. References reflow after the new acknowledgments without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 adds an acknowledgments paragraph, ICLR 2025 publication headers, and a short clarification in Table 3’s caption. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3’s caption is revised, publication headers are added, and the acknowledgments shift the reference layout. Figures, table structures, and appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting accuracy by correcting Section 4.1 to agree with Table 4 and improves reproducibility clarity by explicitly identifying the shared CLIP retriever in Table 3. These are limited, useful improvements; the empirical evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
